description: Build a modular type scale. Pass `base` (px, default 16) and `ratio` (a number from 1.01 to 4, or a name: minor second, major second, minor third, major third, perfect fourth, augmented fourth, perfect fifth, golden, major sixth, octave; default major third 1.25). Optional: `stepsUp` (default 6), `stepsDown` (default 2), `rootPx` (default 16), `minViewport` and `maxViewport` (defaults 320 and 1280), `minBase` and `minRatio` for the small-screen end of the fluid scale (default: same base, ratio pulled 20 percent toward 1). Returns each step with px, rem and a clamp() expression that interpolates linearly between the two viewports, plus fixed and fluid CSS custom properties. The ratio names come from music intervals and are a web design convention, not a law; Bringhurst, The Elements of Typographic Style, discusses scales of related sizes. Pure calculation, nothing is stored.

base.description: Body size in px (8 to 64, default 16).

maxViewport.description: Viewport width in px where the fluid scale reaches full size (default 1280).

minBase.description: Base size at the small viewport (default same as base).

minRatio.description: Ratio at the small viewport, number or name (default: 20 percent closer to 1 than ratio).

minViewport.description: Viewport width in px where the fluid scale uses its small values (default 320).

ratio.description: A number (1.01 to 4) or a name such as "major third", "perfect fourth", "golden". Default major third.

rootPx.description: Root font size for rem conversion (default 16).

stepsDown.description: Steps below the base (0 to 6, default 2).

stepsUp.description: Steps above the base (0 to 12, default 6).

name: modular_scale
title: Modular type scale
